Text: Just got this and opened it tonight, and this merits my first review! Tastes homemade, lots of beef and potatoes, the gravy is wonderful and plentiful if you want to add vegetables or dip biscuits.  It was just what I wanted on a cold rainy winter night.  Got the 38oz so I could use it as dinners, and a half can is ample dinner for someone hungry.  (Beats the heck out of takeout, chinese, pizza or burgers for both price and taste: ca. $2/half can.)  In this recession, a practical gift like this will definitely be appreciated, so If you're looking to send a little something to someone living alone (elderly, students, singles, physically challenged) who work all the time or don't like to cook, this is it! I'm 50+ and have a back injury that makes standing/cooking difficult and painful especially in this weather; but this microwaves in minutes and hits the spot.  I didn't even have to haul it in from the car; delivered free to the doorstep by UPS! I was hesitant this time ordering canned food with the holiday this week, but I got it in 2 days!  You got a customer for life, the price was excellent and delivery faster than I expected!

I've been using Nevella Sucralose to Go ($3 at Wal-Mart vs $6.66 + shipping here), but with Sucralose to Go one "squeeze" equals 1 teaspoon, where with EZ-Sweetz, one DROP equals 1 Tablespoon.

Having now tried EZ-Sweetz, the conversion chart definitely seems to hold true. While it takes 4-5 long squeezes of Sucralose to Go to sweeten a 12-ounce glass of iced tea or a mug of coffee, about 4 drops of EZ-Sweetz provide the same sweetness. So the 2oz bottle of EZ-Sweetz should provide about 4 times as many servings as the 1.68 oz bottle of Sucralose to Go.

Doing the math, even if this lasts about 4 times as long as Sucralose to Go, as long as I only buy Sucralose to Go at Wal-Mart, EZ-Sweetz through Amazon costs SLIGHTLY more.

Also there's no aftertaste, it just sweetens your drinks without the Maltodextrin you get with Splenda.

Chicken and Broccoli Skillets is relatively easy to prepare. Essentially, everything goes in the pan and you simmer for a while. The required chicken breast is not included. The box says preparation time is about 20 minutes, and that seems about correct.

The problem is what happens when the cooking is done.

First, Cheesy Skillets looks unappetizing. The color is off-white and looks absolutely nothing like the picture on the box. The little pieces of broccoli from the box mostly disappear, covered by the cheese sauce. In fact, the whole thing appears to be one color. One way to help the appearance is to throw actual broccoli into the mix.

Second, the flavor is plain. When I say plain, I mean exceedingly plain. I suppose if you are trying to cook in a way that is unlikely to offend anyone, the flavor of this stuff is it. It reminded me of school cafeteria or chow line food. I was able to detect a vague broccoli taste in combination with a mild cheese flavor. Those two flavors were the sum total of the flavor experience. I have no idea how to save the flavor. This bland concoction needs a kick of some kind, but I am not sure what kind. Since this is supposed to be a cheese based product, perhaps jalapenos. Unfortunately, it would take more experimentation than I am interested in conducting.

Third, the rice felt funny in my mouth. I typically eat Asian style rice, which is somewhat sticky and has a nice body to it. The rice in cheesy skillets is difficult to describe. It seemed to have a vague pasta texture or consistency. The rice was definitely slippery.

Many products exist that have sort of base to which you add meat. These product encompass hamburger, tuna, and chicken, at the very least. We have been fans of Velveeta brand cheese for many years. We will not be adding Velveeta Chicken and Broccoli Skillets to our list of favorite foods.

Good luck!

That's when I realized a lot of the small packets were kind of glued together and many of them was solid like a piece of rock candy inside. Usually I would have alerted Amazon right away since Amazon customer service is always number one. However, since I was leaving for the trip, I just salvaged whatever I could for the trip.

Aside from the product quality issue, this sweetener is actually not too bad. It dissolves when poured hot liquid over, or with a few stirs. However, unlike regular Splenda, it does not dissolve easily with cold liquid.

This grind of tea needs to be in an espresso machine or else you will get floaties. I tried this tea three ways: espresso, regular drip coffee, and loose in boiling water and strained later. It had to be strained 3 times to get most of the floaters out of it, and while I'm okay with some actual tea leaves in other brands occasionally making it into the cup, this fine grain floaty stuff really put me off for some reason. Well, I have very mixed emotions (some practical; some pure speculation and some possibly unreasonable) about this particular product. Please note that I have given these treats only three stars...this is over the objection of my dogs who absolutely love these things.

I have four dogs and our family spends much time with them. A lot of time is spent in training and we have found that "treat food" is a wonderful motivator; the more the dogs like the treat, the better they perform.

Now there is no doubt that these are a desirable little jar of goodies as far as the taste of our particular dogs is concerned...there is not problem in this area. I must admit though that I was negligent in doing my research on these things and simply did not read the labeling as I should have done. Thanks to a couple of wonderful reviews here which brought to my attention that these little things are made in CHINA, I no longer use them. Perhaps this is being overly cautious and perhaps being overly zealous is my private little hang-up about only buying American made products when ever possible, but so be it.

While we have had no health problems with our dogs since using this product, it must be noted that there have been several instances (as noted by other reviewers) of tainted animal food coming out of China. If you will note, there have also been quite a number of instances where tainted human baby products have been shipped and sold in this country which were also manufactured in china. Now it would only seem logical to me that if a manufacturing firm or firms made, released and sold products that are harmful to humans, then even less thought would be given to products for "animals." Perhaps I am wrong here, but it is never-the-less how I see it.

Now are dogs are fed these things in very small amounts so the possibility that they would be injured by a product that was actually tainted is slim, but still and all I am not willing to take this chance with the lives of our dogs who are, in all reality, members of our family.

I am also absolutely sick and tired of spending my hard earned money on products that could be and should be manufactured here at home...good grief...this cannot be good for us as a country!

To use these things is of course ultimately the decision of each individual. This is my take on the situation as to the product, and as I said, we will not longer be using it.

Don Blankenship
The Ozarks

I am not a coffee snob. I am, however, a former barista who appreciates coffee that has been properly roasted ground and brewed. When I have company I often am complimented on what a good cup of coffee I've served and delight in explaining to my guests that my secret is fresh, coarse ground beans and a french press. That said I do like Starbucks' Breakfast Blend quite a bit though I prefer medium roasts and have recently discovered an excellent fair trade store brand Columbian that is divine.

Unless I am in the mood for a coffee treat (think Caramel Frappucinos) or a home brewed cappucino I only drink my coffee black. I've loved the smell and taste of coffee since I was far too young to be drinking it so when I drink it I want to taste coffee, not sugar and dairy. A badly made cup of coffee is downright depressing. I won't drink percolated coffee unless there is nothing else available because it tends to destroy the oils in coffee beans that give them a smooth flavor. Same with overly roasted beans. But I'm getting off subject here...

What did I think of Melitta Cafe Collection's Blanc et Noir?

The first thing I noticed when I opened the bag was that I wasn't instantly hit with its scent. Half of what I love about making coffee is what I like to think of as the foreplay... that enticing odor teasing me when I open up the bag! Okay, I guess I can live without it. As this is a very finely ground blend I chose to prepare it as espresso. I would not recommend this coffee to those who use a french press (course ground is best when using that method) as you will end up drinking a LOT of the powdery grind that passes through the mesh of your press which for some can cause digestive upsets and for others is just gross. I did not try percolating it but I'm certain others who will review this product will use that method so check out what they thought if you'd like to know.

I tried Blanc et Noir both as my preferred cuppa, black, and with steamed milk, as a latte. I was expecting a much stronger flavor for such a beautiful dark brew. As a stand-alone cup of black coffee it wasn't overly memorable. Smooth without the bitterness darker roasts often have or the acidic bite of lighter roasts. It sounds good in theory but by combining the two they somehow loose what makes each special. Which is why I tried it with some steamed milk and a little foam as well. I must say that if you like milk in your coffee this is a lovely coffee to pair with it. Unlike traditional espresso which is a dark roast, the added light roast just gave it something I can't seem to find the right word for.

While I don't think Blanc et Noir is one I'd choose for brewing at home given other options I would definitely request it if it were being offered at a coffee house I was patronizing.

I've owned cats for all of my life, and I've tried pretty much any cat treat I find in stores over the years. I'm always game to try something new, to see if my cats will enjoy it. When Amazon Vine had a sample pack of the Petite Cuisine Grilled Tuna Treats on offer, I promptly grabbed up a set to test out.

You get strips of, in essence, real grilled tuna. They come in a resealable pouch. They are fairly expensive.

My cat loves fresh fish and eats a variety of it. However, she just was not interested in this. Maybe because it's one solid chunk of fish. I tried to break it up for her into more easily digestible chunks, but she just wasn't that interested.

I then put the rest in the fridge to try again later. But the resealable pouch didn't do a great job, and she just wasn't interested in eating any more of it.

I have to wonder just why this is better - if you're going to go to the expense of feeding your cat real human-grade tuna - than simply buying tuna for far less at your grocery store and feeding your cat that. It seems extreme to buy this special kitty-version of it.

Certainly I can see that some cats would enjoy fresh tuna. But for a variety of reasons, I don't recommend buying this specialized expensive cat-specific version if that is your aim in life.

There isn't alot of it in the bottle, but the color of the drink combined with the pulp gives the strong impression that something inside went bad (or worse - it gives the impression of looking at pond water with floating bugs and stuff). I don't know why this is not known to everyone, everywhere, but cats should eat a grain free, wet food diet. They cannot digest or get any nutrition from grains, so there is no reason for grains to be in cat food, yet to save money, they put it in. Also, cats naturally have a very low thirst drive, and with the correct diet, they will hardly ever drink water. If they are on a dry kibble diet, they will have to drink to get their water, and with the low thirst drive that is natural, a lot of cats don't get anywhere NEAR the amount of water they need. Cats on a dry food diet are likely to have kidney problems or urinary tract problems that could be prevented just by changing to a wet food diet. This is so important, and I urge everyone who loves their cat to get them off the dry food, and over a couple weeks, switch them to a grain free, wet food diet. Sorry to be preachy, but the word needs to be spread!

This Weruva food is a big hit with my kitty, and it is a proper grain free wet food that makes sure he is getting the water he is supposed to get. Yes, it is canned in Thailand, but it is in an all human grade food facility. I would be much happier if it was all done in the US, but it has been reviewed by reputable sources and scored well. The other bonus, at least with the chicken flavors, is that they smell good! No stinky cat food smell, but in fact smells like something you might want a bite of. The cashier at the pet store I used to get this food from said he had eaten it, and it was good! Of course, it is also important to give them a variety, so I give him some of the "fishy" ones too, but the chicken smells great. I would recommend this food, but whether you feed this one or another one, please feed a grain free wet food diet to your cats!

I was really excited to get these because I've seen babies sucking on these pouches around town. Now that my baby's eating solids, I wanted to see what all the rage is. I love them for many reasons!

-First, they're ORGANIC, no fillers added.

-Second, they TASTE GOOD (of course I tasted!). What's more is my baby loves it more than any food he's tried so far. He couldn't get enough.

-NUTRITIOUS: Baby gets his greens--broccoli and spinach--mixed with sweet pears. You can actually see the green flecks of goodness.

-TEXTURE: Fruits and veggies are well-pureed, perfect for stage 1.

-3 WAYS TO FEED: 1-Squeeze into bowl and spoon feed, 2-Squeeze directly onto spoon, 3-Squeeze into baby's mouth or let baby suck it out through plastic tube.
For the first serving, I mostly spoon fed my baby, but once I let him suck on it, he wanted to keep sucking it down.

-QUANTITY: There's a lot of food in there! 2 servings per pouch, 4.5 oz pouches

-CONVENIENT: Of course it's convenient because you can feed your baby nutritious, organic food without dirtying even one dish or utensil. Convenient because you can feed on the go. Convenient because the cap twists back on so you can save the rest for later...

-The one DRAWBACK would have to be the PRICE. These are pretty expensive for a pouch of food. But it is organic, and for now, I expect to pay more for that.

I'm sold on these, but because of the price, for me, these will be a "sometimes" food bought for convenience and travel. In fact I plan on taking these on vacation with me so I can feed my baby in his stroller, on the run. I'm actually excited to give it a try!

And by the way, after I'm done here, I'll be searching to see what other varieties Baby Gourmet offers...

Happy feeding!

Here's my experience... We have an 80# Golden Retriever who gets overly excited when we have guests. This doesn't exactly fit the "stress" problem that the product is designed for but we thought it might help calm him down a bit particularly when we have guests that aren't dog people and don't care for his enthusiasm. The dosage calls for 1-6 ml depending on weight with the max dose of 6ml for anything over 40#. The first time we tried it we gave 5ml and saw no results. Last night we tried again with 7ml (slightly over recommended dose). Again there was no visible calming. This morning the dog went with me for our usual jog and then back at the house he had some kind of seizure or tremors that lasted about 5 minutes with shaking and very limited, wobbly control of his back legs. By late morning he was his usual self.

So, admittedly we did not use exactly for the intended purpose and did slightly over-dose him although according to directions he could have had another dose after 6 hours and we only gave one. I don't really know that the episode was caused by the product but we've never seen the problem before so it's very suspicious. That's our experience... draw your own conclusions.

The ChocoPerfection "Sugar Free Dark Chocolate Bars" are indeed good tasting, but did cause me to experience some fairly spectacular "gastric distress". I bought a box of these when they came up on Woot and was excited about getting a Maltitol free, diabetic friendly chocolate bar with only 2 net carbs.

While I knew that Maltitol caused me gastric issues, I thought these would be safe since Erythritol is OK for me and ate one before heading out of the house. Sadly I suspect the Oligofructose brought on a very unpleasant reaction that was more than a little embarrassing since it occurred at very public event. Further tests in privacy of my home confirmed that these bars were the cause of the unpleasantness.

Recommended for the flavor and low-carb count, but make sure you know if they will "effect" you before heading out to enclosed places with a lot of people. Ironically, my non-diabetic son doesn't have a reaction to these and enjoys the taste so at least they won't go to waste.
